name: OPNsense
author: Netlens
description: Reads an OPNsense firewall (24.7 or newer): the firewall itself as the gateway node, and every device in its ARP table as a client, with the manufacturer and host name OPNsense knows, enriched with names from the DHCP leases (Dnsmasq or Kea). Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy under the firewall. Read-only: it only sends GET requests with an API key that may only read these lists.

info.title: Make a read-only API key (once)
info.text: In OPNsense: System > Access > Groups > add a group 'netlens' with the privileges listed below, System > Access > Users > add a user 'netlens' in that group (give it a long random password you will not use), then edit the user and press the + under 'API keys': a file with the key and secret is downloaded. Enter them below.
info.code:
Privileges for the group 'netlens' (checked on OPNsense 26.7):
  Diagnostics: ARP Table
  Lobby: Dashboard                    (host name and version)
  Status: Interfaces
  Services: Dnsmasq DNS/DHCP: Settings   (lease list, if Dnsmasq is your DHCP server)
  Services: DHCP: Kea(v4)                (lease list, if you use Kea)

For the health readings (optional; a reading the key may not read is simply left out):
  System: Firmware                     (version and waiting update)
  Diagnostics: Activity                (processor)
  and the Diagnostics privileges that cover the system resources, system time and temperature pages

config.label: Firewalls
config.help: One line per OPNsense. An OPNsense high-availability pair: list both; the first is the gateway.

config.label: Only these interfaces
config.help: Comma separated names as OPNsense shows them (LAN, OPT1 ...). Leave empty for every interface except the WAN.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: OPNsense makes a self-signed certificate until you install your own.

config.label: Read the health of the firewalls
config.help: Processor, memory, temperature, uptime, load, firmware and a waiting update, the interfaces with link, speed and traffic, and the internet interface. A few extra reads per firewall per sync.
